(PER : SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.) :-
1)

By the present Application, the Applicant seek quashing and setting aside of the F.I.R. bearing C.R.No.359/2022 registered with Vashi Police Station, Navi Mumbai for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 323 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The in-laws of Respondent No.2 were also implicated as co- accused in the impugned F.I.R..
Vide this Court Order dated 17/11/2025 in Criminal Application No.637 of 2023, the F.I.R. has been quashed and set- aside qua the in-laws.
Therefore, it is not necessary to refer the allegations made against the in-laws.

Mr.
Khan, the learned APP for Respondent No.1-State and Mr. Deshmukh, the learned Counsel for Respondent No.2.
Perused the Application.
3) The allegations are mainly revolving around the allegations of cruelty, which is punishable under Section 498A of IPC.

As provided in Section 498A, whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

As stated in Explanation appended to this Section, for the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
4) The facts giving rise to this Application are that, the marriage of the Applicant and Respondent No.2 was solemnized on 15/07/2018.
On 30/11/2022, Respondent No.2 filed an oral Report therein she stated that after the marriage, she went to cohabit in the family of the Applicant and her in-laws at Kumbharwada, Navsari, Gujarat.
In August 2018, the Applicant P.H. Jayani 907 APL88.2023.doc wanted to go to Canada to resume his work.
Therefore, the couple had come to the parents' place of Respondent No.2.
At that time, her father wanted to buy a car for her brother.
Therefore, the Applicant also expressed desire that her father should buy a car for him.
However, besides this, the Applicant did not exhibit any conduct that could be rated as the cruelty.
5) In December 2018, when the visa was approved for Respondent No.2, she went to Canada and joined the Applicant.
At that time, they used to reside in rented premises.
Respondent No.2 was not getting a job.
Therefore, the Applicant often get irritated and ask her to bring money from her parents to meet their domestic expenses.
It is alleged that he was telling that her father should set a business for him.
But these acts are not constituting the ingredients of the offence of cruelty.
It is alleged that the Applicant used to taunt her and he stopped her from talking with her friends through a social media platform.
However, the exact taunts are not reproduced in the Report.
Similarly, when the Applicant stopped her from talking with her friends, is not stated in the Report.
It is alleged that the Applicant used to doubt on her but the said doubt is not described in words.
In August, 2019 the Applicant sent the Respondent No.2 back to India to do some professional course.
However, the aforesaid treatment from the Applicant sent her in depression.
However, the depressed condition is not explained by her.

sentences.text: Thereafter the couple took some couple therapy.
Meanwhile, she got a job as a Computer Engineer.
Thereafter, the couple bought a house in their joint name, but, as alleged, the Applicant told Respondent No.2 to demand money from her father to which she refused.
Consequently, the Applicant ransacked in the house and started harassing her.
Yet, the instances of the ransacking are not informed in the Report nor the nature of the alleged harassment is described.
It is stated that, considering said conduct of the Applicant, Respondent No.2 apprehended that either he may hurt to self or to her.
Therefore, she apprised her plight to her father.
In turn, her father gave her Rs.10 lakhs to purchase a house.
Nevertheless, it must be noticed that, the Applicant had not demanded Rs.10 lakhs to Respondent No.2 to be brought from her parents.
Thereafter, the couple came to the matrimonial house at Gujarat to spend some time as a part of counseling/couple therapy.
Thereafter, Respondent No.2 contacted her father and informed him about the alleged cruelty.
Therefore, her father came to Gujarat and brought her to Mumbai.
This was followed by a meeting between the parties and their relatives held in October 2021, at Mumbai.
Then, Respondent No.2 resumed her matrimonial house but after staying there for some days, again the couple went to Canada in October, 2021.
It is alleged that, thereafter, the Applicant used to force her to sign the papers to P.H. Jayani 907 APL88.2023.doc sell the house at Canada.
When she refused, the Applicant threatened to divorce and defame her, and he also assaulted her.

However, the instances of said threatening and the assault are neither stated in the Report nor described with its details.
7) Conspectus of the above discussion is that, except vague and general allegations, there is nothing in the Report against the Applicant so as to conclude that he had subjected Respondent No.2 to 'cruelty' as defined under Section 498A of IPC.
For want of details of the alleged instances of the cruelty, it cannot be said that the Applicant has committed the other offences.

8) Besides, it is important to note that in August 2022, Respondent No.2 filed a divorce petition in Thane Court therein she stated that since 30/03/2021, she and the Applicant were residing separately.
By an e-mail dated 09/06/2022, she conveyed the Applicant the terms of divorce by mutual consent.
On 19/07/2022 , the Applicant filed a divorce Petition in the Court, at Canada.
It was followed by the divorce petition filed by Respondent No.2 on 23/08/2022 in Thane Court.
Thereafter, Respondent No.2 filed the impugned F.I.R. on 30/11/2022.

On 26/03/2024, the Canadian Superior Court of Justice granted a decree of divorce by mutual consent, thereby equalizing the sale proceeds of the house, sale of jewellery, alimony and division of money were finalized as part of the settlement.

However, the said Court imposed on her a costs of CAD 20,000,
for forum P.H. Jayani 907 APL88.2023.doc shopping.
9)

As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent decision between Digambar and Another vs.
the State of Maharashtra and Another1

sentences.text: , mere cruelty is not enough to constitute the offence of Section 498A of I.P.C., as it must be done with the intention to cause grave injury or drive the victim to commit suicide or inflict grave injury to herself.

In the case of Dara Lakshmi Narayana and Others vs. State of Telangana and Another 2, vague allegations of cruelty were levelled in the F.I.R.
by the complainant (wife) and the relatives of the husband (including the parents-in-law) were Vivek Rameshchandra Kataria vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119815277/
3 dragged into the crime without any reason.

sentences.text: The F.I.R. lacked precise allegations and, was lodged after the legal notice for Divorce was sent by the said complainant and it was therefore concluded that the F.I.R. came to be lodged as a retaliatory measure intended to settle score with the husband and his relatives.

10) Considering the facts of the case in hand in the light of the aforesaid reported decisions, it appears that, the Applicant has been booked in this crime only on account of the personal disputes and differences between Respondent No.2 and the Applicant.
Secondly, it appears that, by way of the impugned F.I.R., the Respondent No.2 wanted to pressurize the Applicant and harass him to make him accept her property claims.

Therefore, the continuation of the prosecution arising out of the impugned F.I.R. and the 1 2024 INSC 1019 2. 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3682 P.H. Jayani 907 APL88.2023.doc consequent charge-sheet, would be an abuse of process of law.

Therefore, we are inclined to allow the Application and pass the following Order :-
(a) The proceedings arising out of the impugned F.I.R.
bearing C.R.No.359/2022, registered with Vashi Police Station, Navi Mumbai against the Applicant and the consequent charge- sheet/prosecution, are quashed and set-aside.
(b) Application is disposed of in aforesaid terms.
